title: Perplexity and Intelligence (9 minute read)
summary: Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average. Lower perplexity means better predictions. Perplexity has stood the test of time as a metric many research teams have put a lot of effort into optimizing. It will likely play an important role in standardizing how AI progress is discussed as it continues to deliver consistent gains in general intelligence.

title: Inkling 2 Mini (9 minute read)

title: AI R&D-Relevant Model Capabilities Are Improving Rapidly (29 minute read)
summary: Frontier AI models often match or beat skilled humans on well-defined coding and optimization tasks. The length of tasks they can complete doubles about every 3.6 months. METR says public evidence can't rule out a drastic speedup in AI research within the next couple of years.

title: The Most Important Charts in AI are Wrong (35 minute read)
summary: AI capabilities are starting to become impressive. However, they are still dramatically inferior to what influential AI forecasts and benchmarks have predicted. These forecasts and benchmarks say that we are imminently close to reaching super-intelligence, but the gap between the real world and forecasts keeps growing larger. Now that real-world data exists, it's time to shift from being AI theorists to becoming AI empiricists.

title: Why Post-Training Could Teach Models to Evade Monitoring (3 minute read)

title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron-Labs-Sigma Continuous Diffusion Language Models (5 minute read)

The 8B model supports few-step generation and self-speculative decoding, reaching a 3.46x average throughput speedup over autoregressive decoding on a GB200.

title: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis (3 minute read)

It is expected that the mathematical community will help explain the ideas in the proof in the coming weeks.

title: Building PlanetScale with Insights Agent (6 minute read)
summary: PlanetScale's database optimization agent added an index that made a production query slower because its SQL summary hid a 645-element IN list. Removing that list and filtering the small result set in Ruby cut average query time from 28.5 milliseconds to 1.95 milliseconds. Another change reordered a feature flag check, reducing database lookups from 28.7 million to 8.3 million per day.
